_about: The one project config. Every tool in the kit reads it from the project folder; change this file, never the kit. No secrets here: keys_file only points to where the keys live (a file outside git). Every field except name and site_url is optional: a tool that needs a missing field says which one, and a check that needs one is printed as SKIP, never passed. Keys starting with an underscore are notes.
name: {{name}}
_stack: static (any site: live-page checks only) or nextjs (also runs the checks that read a Next.js repo: kit/adapters/nextjs). Other stacks get 'SKIP <id>: no adapter for <stack>' for those checks.
_site_repo: Folder of the site's code, relative to this folder (or absolute). Empty = no checkout: only the live-page and project checks run.
_site_dir: A static site with no checkout: the folder of its files, relative to this folder. Only used to date the page's last change, so evidence (screenshots, click-through, share preview) can be checked for being newer.
_commit_identity: The git identity commits to the site repo must carry (rule 118). Empty = not checked.
_old_hosts: Retired host names and old server addresses that must never appear in a page, its markup, links or sitemap (rule 78; technical SEO URL-11 and LNK-08).
_spelling: The one spelling the whole site uses (rule 93). Only en-US has a word list; any other value makes that check SKIP.
_keys_file: Path of the keys file, outside git (for example ~/.config/growth/<site>.env, mode 600). Never put a key in this file.

connectors._about: Each connector is off until you switch it on AND its keys are in keys_file. A missing key gives one plain note, never a crash.

_timezone: The zone the owner reads times in (for example America/New_York). Journal, tasks and the release line use it.
_conversion_path: The one page every call to action leads to (booking, quote or contact).
_booking_hosts: Extra outside booking hosts that must never be linked directly (a pasted booking link breaks rule 32). Well-known hosts (Calendly, Cal.com, Zoom, HubSpot meetings) are always checked.
_design: How the gate finds this site's page parts when its markup has no semantic signal (landmarks, ARIA, schema.org, <time datetime>, rel=author): {concept: CSS selector}. Concepts: site_header, site_footer, main, cover_image, byline, updated_date, reading_aid, faq_section, faq_question, table_source, calculator, read_next, disclosure. Selectors: tag, .class, #id, [attr], [attr=v], [attr^=v], [attr*=v], descendant (space), comma lists (kit/tools/gatelib/design.py).
_design_exceptions: A gate check that does not fit this site's design, or a site-wide fault tracked as its own task: [{"check": "<id>", "why": "<reason>", "task": "T5", "until": "2026-12-31"}]. Printed as a WARN with the reason in every gate run; it FAILs again once the task is done or the date has passed. An entry without a reason does nothing.
_disclosure_pattern: A regular expression that matches this site's own 'who we are' line in a review or comparison, when the business does not make the tools it compares (for example a partner or reseller): rule 16.
_box_ignore: Components whose numbers are computed or shared, skipped by claims.box-numbers: [{"selector": ".price-calculator", "why": "its sums are computed from the table above"}]. Anything marked data-calculator is skipped always.
_booking_allowed: The site's OWN booking links that it uses on purpose, each {"match": "<part of the link>", "why": "<the reason>"}, for example {"match": "calendly.com/example-team/", "why": "the booking dialog's 'Pick a time' button opens it"}. Rule 32 then prints a WARN naming the exception instead of a FAIL; any other booking link still FAILs.

cta._about: The one call to action. label: the one text on every primary button. contact_path: the plain contact page. reason_words: words a reason line beside a button talks about (regex alternatives). events, components: dataLayer events and shared components the Next.js adapter looks for. color, color_pressed, color_token: the one CTA colour (Next.js adapter).

features._about: House components some sites have and some do not. A rule about a part you do not have is printed as SKIP. Turn one on (true, or an object with its settings) once the site has it.

nextjs._about: Only for stack nextjs: how this site's code is laid out, so the adapter's checks fit it. Every key is optional; a check that needs a setting you leave empty prints SKIP with the key to set. production_branch and remote: the branch the site is published from (default main, else master; default remote origin; with no such remote the local branch is used). start_date: when the project began (default: the steps log's first row, else the first commit). content_reader: the one module that reads the content files (rule 104). retired_paths: address prefixes that answer 410 on purpose, for example ["/tag"] (rule 76). redirect_files: files holding the redirects (rules 75 and the link map). posts_dir, pages_dir: the Markdown folders (default content/posts, content/pages). hub_files, template_files, related_posts_file, related_generic_tags: see kit/adapters/nextjs/link_map.py.

words._about: The business's own word lists, as regular-expression alternatives. Empty = that check is SKIP.

_silos: Topic sections: {"first-folder-of-the-address": "Label"}. Each silo's top page is a money page.
_old_brand_words: Words of a previous brand or site, as 'one|two'. Doctor A2 and the word check fail while any is left in the project folder or the built site (build_dir). Lines that ban the words (BRAND.md 'never ...') and the steps log, which quotes the owner, do not count.
_build_dir: The folder of the site's production build (for example dist or out), relative to site_repo or absolute. Doctor A2 searches its pages for old_brand_words. Empty = the site is not searched (site_dir is used for a static site with no checkout).

market._about: Asked first in onboarding. Every search, AI-answer check and keyword volume uses the primary market unless a check says otherwise.

_default_author: {"name": "", "role": "", "path": "/author/<slug>", "slug": ""}: the one author every page names (rule 36l). Empty = SKIP.

schema_types._about: The schema.org type of a money page's main node (rule 95). Set the one type the business is (Service for a service company). Organization, WebSite, BreadcrumbList and WebPage never count, because every page carries them.

_preview_url: The one address the owner sees previews on. Empty = the golden-rule guard (ready, url_guard) is off.
